correctness.rationale: Static forts give an if-and-only-if failure criterion; counting the explicit forts proves \(c_A(3)=10,\ c_B(3)=12,\ c_A(4)=14,\ c_B(4)=13\). An edge-count argument excludes two-seed success. Exact complete enumeration of all connected labelled graphs up to order six proves minimality; vertex permutation counts and orbit-stabilizer prove uniqueness of the reversing unlabelled pair. Direct algebra gives \(p^3(1-p)^2(3p-2)\). Standalone checker replay succeeded and separately matched static-fort and dynamic-closure profiles.

value.rationale: A degree sequence and finite seeding budget are naturally central to network diffusion planning. The theorem gives the first and uniquely determined connected degree-preserving structural failure of budget-independent reliability ranking. It identifies a concrete reinforcement mechanism (parallel paths versus two tightly clustered groups with a bridge) and a precise independent-seeding crossover, beyond a routine known-table recomputation. The conclusion is limited to its mathematical model and makes no empirical forecast.
